subject: Observability egress orchestration for on-prem FinTrust — initial handoff
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: David Jones <david.jones@fintrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Observability egress orchestration for on-prem FinTrust — initial handoff

Hi David / FinTrust SecOps team,

Thanks again for the sync today. As discussed, we want to kick off a short handoff so our on-prem telemetry can be routed into your SIEM with no public egress from your private subnet. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm the allowed egress patterns (bastion-only, specific hostnames/IPs, or S3 presigned PUT)
- Preferred SIEM intake (Splunk HEC, QRadar Syslog, Sumo Logic HTTP) and ports
- Any TLS/cipher requirements and mutual-auth expectations (mTLS, client certs)
- Retention and PII scrubbing rules we should apply before shipping

We have two implementation patterns we'd like to propose in the PoC:

1) Forwarder-proxy: our lightweight forwarder runs in the customer's VPC and forwards encrypted payloads to a customer-managed bastion/gateway. This supports HEC/OTLP and preserves trace/span context.
2) Staged upload: redwood packages telemetry bundles and uploads to a customer-controlled S3 endpoint or on-prem gateway (signed PUT), where FinTrust's pipeline pulls and ingests into SIEM.

I'll attach a short handshake checklist and a sample export (see attachments) so you can validate the fields and example payloads.

Proposed immediate next step: if you can confirm the allowed egress host/port pattern and whether you prefer HEC vs presigned uploads, Diego and Kimberly will draft the PoC runbook and a minimal firewall rule set.

Thanks,

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0188

Attachments: handshake-checklist.pdf, export-sample.json

From: David Jones <david.jones@fintrust.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-security@fintrust.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress orchestration for on-prem FinTrust — initial handoff

On Tue, Oct 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi David / FinTrust SecOps team,
> 
> Thanks again for the sync today. As discussed, we want to kick off a short handoff so our on-prem telemetry can be routed into your SIEM with no public egress from your private subnet. High-level asks from our side:

Thanks, Sean — good notes. A few constraints from our side we need to surface up-front:

- No direct public outbound to third-party SaaS endpoints is permitted from our production subnets. All egress must transit through our bastion / egress gateway (10.4.2.11) or an internal S3-compatible staging bucket behind the gateway.
- Preferred ingestion is Splunk HEC (TLS) or a pull-based S3 workflow. We are not allowing persistent TCP connections from foreign hosts unless initiated from the bastion.
- TLS: we require TLS1.2+ with client cert authentication for HEC. mTLS is the preferred pattern for automation.
- Data governance: events with user identifiers should be hashed at source; we can provide a scrubbing guide if needed.

For the PoC, we can open a temporary rule to the bastion IP for HEC over 8088 from a short list of Redwood forwarder IPs (we will provide). Alternatively, if Redwood can produce a signed PUT artifact to our internal S3 endpoint, we prefer that for initial validation.

I'll loop in ops-security@fintrust.com to keep this on their radar.

-David
David Jones
Director, Security Engineering — FinTrust
David.Jones@fintrust.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress orchestration for on-prem FinTrust — initial handoff

Thanks for the details, David — this is helpful.

Internal notes / proposed approach for PoC:

- Default to Splunk HEC over TLS with client certs (matches FinTrust preference). We'll run the forwarder-proxy in the customer's private subnet and terminate TLS at the bastion. Forwarder will be configured to use tag-based sampling for traces and OTLP export for spans.
- Telemetry scrubbing: apply PII hashing and key-redaction hooks before bundling. We'll use our sampling rules to keep trace volume under the agreed SLA.
- Rollout steps: 1) PoC config and test bundle (week 0), 2) Short-lived firewall rule (week 1), 3) Canary ingest (10% hosts) with trace verification (week 2), 4) Full rollout and automation of cert rotation (week 4).
- Observability hooks: we will preserve trace/span IDs in the HEC payload and include an "x-redwood-trace-sampled" header for debugging. OTLP endpoints will mirror HEC payloads for downstream trace storage.

Diego — can you validate compatibility with HEC over 8088 and outline the minimal config we need to hand to FinTrust for the firewall rule and cert install? I attached an orchestration diagram and a trimmed export sample so we can all align on fields.

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: egress-orchestration-diagram.svg

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, David Jones <david.jones@fintrust.com>, ops-security@fintrust.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress orchestration for on-prem FinTrust — initial handoff

Forwarding David's constraints below for context.

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 11:03 AM David Jones <david.jones@fintrust.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Sean — good notes. A few constraints from our side we need to surface up-front:
> 
> - No direct public outbound to third-party SaaS endpoints is permitted from our production subnets. All egress must transit through our bastion / egress gateway (10.4.2.11) or an internal S3-compatible staging bucket behind the gateway.

Implementation notes / firewall/config checklist (for PoC):

- If we proceed with Splunk HEC via bastion: FinTrust to open TCP 8088 from bastion (10.4.2.11) to internal HEC listener (10.4.10.25:8088). Redwood forwarder will connect to bastion on 10.4.2.11:8443 (TLS). We'll present client certs that FinTrust will trust (we'll share CA bundle).
- Certs: Redwood will provide a short-lived client cert + CA chain for PoC. Long term we will automate cert rotation via the customer's ACME or vault integration (deliverable in rollout week 4).
- OTLP/tracing: we'll ship OTLP via the same TLS channel. Sampling decision will be honored by the forwarder and we will surface a sampling rate metric for the FinTrust SREs to monitor.
- Alternative: presigned S3 PUT — Redwood can create gzipped bundles every 5 minutes and upload to internal S3 staging (preferred by FinTrust). For that flow we will need S3 endpoint URL and an IAM/user that can PUT; no inbound firewall change required.

Next steps / action items:

1) FinTrust: confirm preferred PoC path (HEC-through-bastion or presigned-PUT) and provide the S3 endpoint or agree to the temporary firewall rule.
2) Redwood: we will prepare a minimal runbook and share a CA bundle + client cert for PoC.
3) Create REINF-542 in Jira for the PoC; linking the runbook and test vectors.

I'll draft the minimal firewall text that FinTrust can paste into their ticket:
- Source: 10.4.2.11 (bastion)
- Destination: 10.4.10.25:8088 (Splunk HEC)
- Protocol: TCP
- Description: Temporary PoC allowlist for Redwood forwarder via bastion

David / ops-security: if that looks right, can you open the ticket and tag ops-security? We can target test ingest by next Tuesday if cert exchange happens this week.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
